questions.question: According to Brønsted-Lowry, a base is defined as:
options: A substance that produces hydroxide ions in water

questions.question: Which observation exposes a weakness of the Arrhenius definitions?
options: Nitric acid dissolves readily in water
Ammonia solution is basic although NH₃ contains no hydroxide

questions.question: In HNO₃ + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + NO₃⁻, the water molecule acts as:
options: A base, because it accepts the proton
An acid, because it forms hydronium
An ampholyte in this single equation

questions.question: In NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻, water is classified as an acid because it:
The two members of a conjugate acid-base pair differ by:
In HNO₃ + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + NO₃⁻, the conjugate base of HNO₃ is:
The two conjugate pairs in NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ are:
H₂CO₃ and CO₃²⁻ are NOT a conjugate pair because:
options: They never appear in the same equation
They differ by two protons instead of one

subtopics.title: Ampholytes, and the Three Reactions of Acids

questions.question: An amphiprotic substance (ampholyte) is one that:
options: Can donate a proton in one reaction and accept a proton in another
Always forms two salts at once

questions.question: Which pair of equations proves HCO₃⁻ is an ampholyte?
options: HCO₃⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CO₃²⁻ + H₃O⁺ and HCO₃⁻ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ + OH⁻
HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻ → CO₃²⁻ + H₂O and its reverse
H₂CO₃ ⇌ H₂O + CO₂ in both directions

questions.question: An acid reacting with a metal carbonate produces:
The correctly balanced equation for nitric acid reacting with calcium oxide is:
Bromothymol blue in a neutral solution is:
The indicator that is colourless in acid and pink in base is:
Litmus paper dipped into a basic solution turns:
Acid is dripped into a basic solution containing bromothymol blue. The colour sequence observed is:
In the pass-the-ball picture of acid-base chemistry, the ball is:
Ammonia qualifies as a base despite containing no hydroxide because it:
options: Is a good proton catcher, and hydroxide is created from the water it takes the proton from

questions.question: To find the acid in any equation, look for the species that:
options: Loses an H going from left to right
Gains an H going from left to right

subtopics.title: Partners Across the Pass, and the Player Who Plays Both Sides

questions.question: A conjugate pair is best pictured as:
options: Two teammates on the same side of the equation
An acid and any base it reacts with
The same player photographed before and after the pass — with and without the proton

questions.question: Water plays opposite roles against nitric acid and against ammonia because:
options: Its role depends on its opponent — it catches from a strong donor and throws to a keen catcher
It decomposes differently in each case

questions.question: The instruction "show that HCO₃⁻ is an ampholyte" requires:
options: One equation with a double arrow
Two equations — one where it donates a proton and one where it accepts one
A list of its physical properties
The equation for carbon dioxide dissolving

subtopics.title: Three Fizzes and Four Colour Changes

questions.question: Which base partner gives off a gas when it reacts with an acid?
options: A metal carbonate, which releases carbon dioxide

questions.question: Vinegar foaming on baking soda and acid fizzing on limestone are both examples of:
options: Acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide

questions.question: The only one of the four required indicators with a distinct neutral colour is:
options: Bromothymol blue, which is green at neutral
Litmus, which is purple at neutral
Phenolphthalein, which is grey at neutral
Methyl orange, which is white at neutral

questions.question: Neutralisation produces water because:
options: The acid's protons combine with the base's hydroxide: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O
